newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kyrgyz leader sacks senior officials.
newsitem.headline: Kyrgyz leader sacks senior officials.

text.p: Kyrgyz President Askar Akayev has sacked his country's top customs official and two regional governors for "serious violations of financial discipline" -- a term usually meaning corruption.
A presidential spokesman, contacted by telephone from the Kazakh capital Almaty, said the decision was taken following a recommendation by Kyrgyzstan's Security Council.

The Security Council, an inner circle of top state and defence officials, met on Thursday and examined law and order issues in the Central Asian state. On Friday it was due to consider the problem of drug-trafficking.

The spokesman gave no details of the meeting or of the reasons behind Akayev's decree sacking the head of the state customs inspectorate, Anatoly Lemeshchenko, and the governors of the Issyk-Kul and Naryn regions.
Akayev also dismissed the heads of three regional administrations and gave a severe reprimand to First Deputy Prime Minister Abdyzhapar Tagayev and to Deputy Prime Minister Bekbolat Talgarbekov.
Other regional officials were also reprimanded.
